# freshdesk_sla_policy (Resource)

An SLA policy setting response and resolution targets for the tickets it matches.

~> The Freshdesk API offers no way to delete an SLA policy. Destroying this resource removes it from state and warns; the policy itself stays until it is deleted in the portal. Set `active = false` to stop it applying.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "freshdesk_sla_policy" "premium" {
  name        = "Premium customers"
  description = "Tighter targets for customers on the premium tier"
  active      = true

  applicable_to_company_ids = [freshdesk_company.northwind.id]

  # Every duration is in seconds.
  sla_target = {
    priority_1 = { respond_within = 14400, resolve_within = 172800, next_respond_within = 14400 }
    priority_2 = { respond_within = 7200, resolve_within = 86400, next_respond_within = 7200 }
    priority_3 = { respond_within = 3600, resolve_within = 43200, next_respond_within = 3600 }
    priority_4 = { respond_within = 900, resolve_within = 14400, next_respond_within = 900 }
  }
}

resource "freshdesk_company" "northwind" {
  name = "Northwind Traders"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the policy.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the policy is in force.
- `applicable_to_company_ids` (Set of Number) Restrict the policy to tickets from these companies.
- `applicable_to_group_ids` (Set of Number) Restrict the policy to tickets in these groups.
- `applicable_to_product_ids` (Set of Number) Restrict the policy to tickets on these products.
- `applicable_to_sources` (Set of Number) Restrict the policy to tickets from these source channels.
- `applicable_to_ticket_types` (Set of String) Restrict the policy to these ticket types.
- `description` (String) Description of the policy.
- `escalation` (String) Escalation recipients as a JSON object, keyed by the target being missed.
- `position` (Number) Evaluation order. The first matching policy wins, so lower positions take precedence.
- `sla_target` (Attributes Map) Targets keyed by priority: `priority_1` (low) through `priority_4` (urgent). All durations are in seconds. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--sla_target))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the policy was created (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) Numeric identifier of the policy.
- `is_default` (Boolean) Whether this is the fallback policy applied when no other matches.
- `updated_at` (String) When the policy was last changed (RFC 3339).

<a id="nestedatt--sla_target"></a>
### Nested Schema for `sla_target`

Required:

- `resolve_within` (Number) Seconds allowed to resolve the ticket.
- `respond_within` (Number) Seconds allowed for the first response.

Optional:

- `business_hours` (Boolean) Whether the clock counts business hours only, rather than calendar hours.
- `escalation_enabled` (Boolean) Whether missing a target raises an escalation.
- `next_respond_within` (Number) Seconds allowed for each follow-up response. Must be at least 30 when set.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by numeric ID.
terraform import freshdesk_sla_policy.example 42
```
